title: PR #54871 added a user notification-option DELETE endpoint that looks up the NotificationSettingOption by id without restricting it to the URL's user, so any user can delete other users' alert notification settings.

findings.explanation: The code uses Django ORM methods (objects.get, objects.filter, update_or_create) which utilize parameterized queries by default. There is no raw SQL execution or string concatenation of user input into SQL statements.

The `delete` method in `UserNotificationOptionsDetailEndpoint` fetches a `NotificationSettingOption` using only the `id` provided in the URL (`notification_option_id`). It does not verify that the `user_id` of the fetched object matches the authenticated user (`request.user` or the `user` parameter passed from the URL). This allows any authenticated user to delete notification options belonging to other users by guessing or enumerating IDs (IDOR).
findings.suggested_fix: Add a filter to the query to ensure the object belongs to the current user: `NotificationSettingOption.objects.get(id=notification_option_id, user_id=user.id)`.
